title: The normalized theta difference bundle pulls back to the Picard family
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g\geq1$ [def-sc-curves, def-kun-projective, def-sc-genus], let $P\in C(k)$, and fix its Jacobian $J$ with the representing isomorphism [def-sc-jacobian]. Put $f_P(Q)=[\mathcal O_C(Q-P)]$, and let $\mathcal M_P$ be the universal degree-zero Picard sheaf normalized along $P\times J$ and $C\times0$. Let $\Theta=W_{g-1}\subset J$ be the scheme-theoretic image of the effective divisors $D$ of degree $g-1$ by $D\mapsto[\mathcal O_C(D-(g-1)P)]$, using the constructions of [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry]. Let $\Theta^-=[-1]_J^*\Theta$, let $L=\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-)$, and on $J\times J$ put $L_0=m^*L\otimes p_1^*L^{-1}\otimes p_2^*L^{-1}$, normalized along the identity axes. Then there is an isomorphism of invertible sheaves, with the indicated normalizations,
$$(f_P\times[-1]_J)^*L_0\cong\mathcal M_P.$$
Here $m$ is addition, $p_1,p_2$ the projections, and $[-1]_J$ inversion; all sheaves are invertible sheaves in the sense of [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Chapter III Lemma 6.8(b), printed p.106, with Theta^- (the inversion image of Theta), not Theta. Its proof uses Lemma 6.7 and the see-saw theorem I 5.16 and I 5.19; the concluding equality is the bundle identity needed in Lemma 6.9.

proof.text: First check the product-family hypotheses used below. The curve $C$ is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-component-pure-transcendental] to $C$ and the rational point $P$: its residue field is $k=k(u_1,\ldots,u_0)$, and its connected component is all of $C$. Thus $C$ is geometrically integral. By the definitions of a Jacobian and an abelian variety, $J$ is proper and smooth over $k$; properness explicitly includes separatedness and finite type. Thus the parameter $T=J$ satisfies all three parameter hypotheses of the see-saw theorem used in step 5. For $q:C\times J\to J$ the section is $a\mapsto(P,a)$, and the fibre over $s\in J$ is the base change $C_{\kappa(s)}$, which is integral by the definition of geometric integrality [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The projection $q$ is the base change of the proper morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ along $J\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]; flatness follows on product affines because a $k$-basis of a coordinate algebra of $C$ makes its tensor product with a coordinate algebra of $J$ free over the latter. The smoothness of $C/k$ includes local finite presentation by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; these local finite presentations base change to $J$ by tensoring their generators and relations. Hence $q$ is proper, flat, locally of finite presentation and has geometrically integral fibres.

source.place: III 6.8, product C times J; geometric hypotheses for I 5.16 and I 5.19.

proof.text: Put $h=f_P\times[-1]_J$, $p:C\times J\to C$, and $\mathcal A=h^*m^*L$. On the fibre at $a$, the composite with addition is $Q\mapsto f_P(Q)-a=t_{-a}f_P(Q)$. Thus $\mathcal A_a=f_P^*\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-+a)$: pull a local Cartier equation of $\Theta^-$ back along the automorphism $t_{-a}$, so that $t_{-a}^*\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-)=\mathcal O_J(t_{-a}^*\Theta^-)$ for the associated invertible module of the effective Cartier divisor [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], and then along $f_P$. Apply [lem-sfb-generic-theta-abel-cartier-pullback] to obtain $\mathcal A_a\cong\mathcal O_C(D(a))$ for $a\in U(k)$, where $[\mathcal O_C(D(a)-gP)]=a$. Since $\mathcal M_P$ represents the identity Picard family by [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry], its fibre at this point is $\mathcal O_C(D(a)-gP)$. Consequently $\mathcal A_a\cong(\mathcal M_P)_a\otimes\mathcal O_C(gP)$. The last tensor identity can be checked at each point by multiplying the local fractional generators $t^{-n}$ of the divisor sheaves; their exponents add.

source.place: III 6.7 and III 6.8, first paragraph and fibre calculation.

proof.text:
Consider the invertible sheaf $\mathcal H=\mathcal M_P\otimes p^*\mathcal O_C(gP)\otimes\mathcal A^{-1}$ on $C\times J$. Its trivial-fibre locus $Z\subseteq J$ is closed by [lem-sc-picard-fiber-triviality-closed], applied to $q$ with the hypotheses checked in step 1. Step 2 puts $U(k)\subseteq Z$. The open subscheme $U$ of $J$ is smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: local finite presentation restricts to opens, and any lift across a first-order thickening still lands in $U$, since that thickening does not change the underlying topological space, so [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] says $U(k)$ is dense in $U$; since $U$ is dense in $J$, its closure in $J$ is $J$. Therefore $Z=J$. In particular, for every $a\in J(k)$,
$$\mathcal A_a\cong(\mathcal M_P)_a\otimes\mathcal O_C(gP).$$

source.place: III 6.8(a), applying I 5.19 to the comparison sheaf.

proof.text:
At $a=0$, $\mathcal A_0=f_P^*L$ and $(\mathcal M_P)_0\cong\mathcal O_C$, so step 3 gives $f_P^*L\cong\mathcal O_C(gP)$. Now put $\mathcal B=h^*L_0$. For any $a\in J(k)$ the three tensor factors defining $L_0$ give
$$\mathcal B_a\cong\mathcal A_a\otimes(f_P^*L)^{-1}\otimes(L^{-1}|_{-a})_C.$$
The last factor is a constant one-dimensional $k$-line and is therefore isomorphic to $\mathcal O_C$. Substitute step 3 and the identity at $0$ and cancel $\mathcal O_C(gP)$ against its inverse. This gives $\mathcal B_a\cong(\mathcal M_P)_a$ for every $a\in J(k)$. Constant lines are retained in the global bundle; this fibre calculation does not discard a possible line bundle on $J$.

source.place: III 6.8, the specialization a=0 and the three restrictions of the difference bundle.

proof.text: Since $f_P(P)=0$, the map $h$ on $P\times J$ lands in $0\times J$. The stipulated identity-axis normalization of $L_0$ therefore trivializes $\mathcal B|_{P\times J}$. Use this trivialization and the stipulated trivialization of $\mathcal M_P|_{P\times J}$ to specify an isomorphism along $P\times J$. Apply [lem-sfb-rigidified-product-seesaw] with $V=C$, $x=P$, $T=J$, $\mathcal E=\mathcal B$, and $\mathcal F=\mathcal M_P$. Step 1 supplies proper geometric integrality and smoothness of the parameter, and step 4 supplies all fibre isomorphisms. This yields an isomorphism $h^*L_0\cong\mathcal M_P$ extending precisely the chosen normalization along $P\times J$.

source.place: III 6.8(b), I 5.16 and restriction to P times J.

proof.text: Finally $h(C\times0)$ lies in $J\times0$, so the other identity-axis normalization trivializes $\mathcal B|_{C\times0}$, as does the prescribed normalization of $\mathcal M_P|_{C\times0}$. The normalized isomorphism between these trivial sheaves and the restriction of the isomorphism of step 5 agree at $(P,0)$: the two axis normalizations are compatible there. Apply uniqueness in [lem-sfb-rigidified-product-seesaw] once more, with $V=C$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $x=P$. The two isomorphisms on $C\times0$ are equal. Thus the global isomorphism respects both indicated normalizations.

proof_origin.place: Chapter III Lemma 6.8(a),(b), pp.105–106; I 5.16–5.19, p.26. Normalized uniqueness made explicit.
